newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Marks, dlrs for Asian issuers.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Marks, dlrs for Asian issuers.

text.p: Ka Wah Bank took marks while other Asian issuers stuck with dollars in a moderately busy Asian debt day on Wednesday.

Hong Kong's Ka Wah Bank launched a 135 million mark floating rate note issue via Dresdner Bank. The five-year notes were priced and re-offered at 99.90 to float at 50 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate. Fees are 10 basis points.
Bankers said the deal pays an all-in of roughly 55 basis points in marks, or about 57.5 basis points in dollar terms.
They said that pricing was a mite tight compared with the 58 basis points Ka Wah paid for a three-year floating rate certificate of deposit issue launched in late February.
Nevertheless, they said the issue might appeal to German banks that may be interested in taking on Hong Kong exposure.
Further details emerged on Mancon's US$100 million FRN, which was launched via Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The five-year deal has puts in years three and four and pays a coupon of 150 basis points over LIBOR. Fees are 75 basis points flat.
Some details also were out on Rizal Commercial Bank's two-tranche FRCD issue due next week, as well as on Pacific Electric Wire and Cable Co's US$100 million FRN.

Bankers in Hong Kong said the drop in the dollar following the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision on Tuesday to hold interest rates steady could put a damper on fixed-rate bond issuance by Asian borrowers.

"The strength of the Japanese yen against the U.S. dollar causes some problems for Japanese investors, which are particularly big in Asian bond markets, because for them the valuations have changed," said Raja V, research manager at BA Asia in Hong Kong.
"Now a dollar investment looks like a money loser and that comes at a pretty bad time for Asia when countries like Thailand and Korea require a lot of investment through bonds," he said.
The dollar dropped a full yen to 112.65 by the end of U.S. trading. In late Asian trade, the dollar had recoverd to 113.68 yen, but remained well below levels touched earlier this week.
U.S. economists had been split on whether the Fed would raise rates at Tuesday's meeting, but many have forecast a tightening before year-end.
With that in mind, bankers said some Asian issuers may opt to raise fixed-rate funds soon rather than risk the possibility of higher rates later, even with a weaker dollar.
The Fed policy group meets again on July 1 and 2.
Indonesian fishery products producer Daya Guna launched a US$225 million fixed-rate bond today.
The 10-year bond can be called after five years and is expected to be priced at 335-345 basis points over comparable Treasuries.

In the loan markets, banks are bidding for a mandate to arrange a HK$7-8 billion financing for a joint project by Swire Pacific Ltd's Swire Properties Ltd and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd's (N.T) Properties Ltd, bankers said on Wednesday.
The loan is expected to have a tenor of four years.
Bankers said they expect the financing to be launched this week for the initial funding of the redevelopment of the former Shui Wing steel mill in Hong Kong's Tseung Kwan O.
